correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and centrally symmetric C-infinity positive-curvature bases, the exact section/strip graph Jacobian proves the polar facet identity. Smooth Morse coordinates at every unique support point give the cap coefficient 2^(n/2)*kappa_(n-2)/(n sqrt(GaussCurvature)), which doubles for the two symmetric caps. Transfer through the nondegenerate rim coordinate yields precisely the stated C(v)>0. The one-sided power has sharp C^(k,alpha) regularity and is smooth elsewhere. Reproducibility checks cover 266 numerical instances but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The actual axial face of the section-volume body is a scaled polar copy of an arbitrary smooth symmetric prism base, a natural geometric invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter restriction. The precise attachment law identifies how Gauss curvature controls the first deviation of the side wall from that face and yields a globally sharp dimension-dependent Hölder regularity classification. This structural result exceeds the classical round-cylinder area formula and identifies behavior relevant to geometric tomographic smoothing.
